quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and help guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of wrecked vehicles.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, it is important to remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on an incline than smaller vehicles do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: The most effective thing you can do to reduce your risk of being injured or killed in a traffic crash is to:

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best way to reduce your risk of death or injury in a car crash.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and get through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for it to pass before you proceed.

questions.question: Night driving can be more difficult than driving during the day because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.explanation: Alcohol slows brain activity and reduces your driving skills. It makes your reaction time slower and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: A person's ability to drive can be impaired by:

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
A lack of sleep.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical condition. Alcohol, medications, and tiredness can all impair your driving ability.

questions.question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:

options.text: Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure all of the vehicle's occupants have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure all of the vehicle's occupants have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not put too much thought into it because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Disregard any obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes before driving to familiarize yourself with the operation and location of all the vehicle's equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes before driving to familiarize yourself with the operation and location of all the vehicle's equipment.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Increase your speed.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers of your plan.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.
The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.
One driver should continue driving without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that turning right is not allowed at this location.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine makes both stronger. For example, one drink plus cold medicine can affect you like several drinks alone.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:

options.text: Road hazard sign.
Interstate route sign.
School crossing sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are usually yellow or orange. They warn you about hazards ahead or special rules in that area.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
questions.explanation: Always use your signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from the curb. This is the law.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: The speed your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the pavement.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: How far your vehicle travels when braking depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the road surface.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness make it harder to focus on driving. If you are upset, it is better to wait before driving.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with a fist of space between it and your chest.

questions.question: Signaling your intentions before turning, changing lanes, or driving away from a curb:

options.text: Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
Is not necessary if the maneuver is done slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Always signal before pulling away from the curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you false confidence.
It reduces your thinking ability.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It makes you feel overly confident. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, hurts your coordination and balance, and makes it harder to judge distances. This makes it difficult to react quickly to what happens around you.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police immediately.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and move away from them. Trying to get back at an aggressive driver makes the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says something different.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws and ignore construction.

questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from flaggers and signs in construction zones. Not following their directions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.
